title: Guarded Runner Start Readiness Review
claim: Guarded runner start remains blocked after FP-MCP-274: the preview tool is live, but execution is not ready because global execution disable is active, runner/OpenCode execution are disabled, and no fresh request, approval, clearance, or preflight tuple exists for a future guarded start.
summary: FP-MCP-275 performed a non-executing readiness review after the clearance review manifest preview tool was implemented and live-surfaced. ForgePilot core and the MCP bridge started clean. The read-only execution gate orientation showed the remote runner capabilities endpoint is reachable and advertises a callable guarded start capability with requirements for approval evidence, preflight, disable-switch clearance, request artifact hash, target execution commit, evidence ledger validation, and pre/post state recording. However, execution is not allowed now: the global disable switch is active, runner execution is disabled, OpenCode execution is disabled, and there is no fresh request artifact, approval artifact, local clearance, or guarded preflight for FP-MCP-275. This packet records readiness state only. It does not attempt to create or approve clearance, clear the disable switch, contact the runner start endpoint, start OpenCode, submit a prompt, call wait, or run a canary.
caveats: The execution gate orientation was read-only and used FP-MCP-275 as observational context, not as an execution packet.
The orientation reported contract incomplete before the checkpoint because packets/FP-MCP-275.md did not exist yet at the time of the orientation call.
The orientation also saw repo state invalid while trace artifacts were intentionally uncommitted; those traces were then committed before this checkpoint.
A fresh scoped execution tuple must be created for any future guarded start; stale historical tuples remain unsuitable.
